notes: source.mutex.guard.v1: a second `mutex guards` over an already protected footprint is refused at Q617 FootprintAlreadyProtected, so no composite protocol is admitted; the refused generation is then unknown to the scope-exit destruction (Q600 UnknownMutex). The refusal is about the shared payload, not about the number of mutexes: the disjoint_payloads control declares two generations over two disjoint payloads and is accepted, so this rejection is not the vacuous rule `at most one mutex`. That control compiles through the Linux emission path, which is why this case records evidence_target=linux even though the rejection itself is host-independent. Not established: any composite/nested protection protocol, lock ordering, or protection that grows after creation.
